The ultimate vodka, made to a special 100 year old recipe is going back on the market for the firs time in a century Đin a gold bottle with a Ű100,000 Euros price tag / Ł80,000 GBP / 7,000 USD.
Three kilos of gold-plated silver will be used for each bottle of RussoBaltique Vodka , Off Road Edition, which is blended with freshly gathered Alpine snow.
The vodka was born in the winter of 1912 by the manufacturer of the late Russo-Baltique motor car company
.
Three bottles were kept in a holder next to the passengerŐs door of a Russo-Baltique C24-55 for the1912 Monaco rally for the drivers to celebrate the finish of the arduous race and to help keep warm driving an open top car in temperatures as low as minus 30 degrees.
In 2009, a surviving bottle of the original three  was offered to Prince Albert of Monaco at the Top Marques luxury car show at the Grimaldi Forum in Monaco.
This new version comes in a stunning decanter set in gold that recreates the radiator guard from the early  Russo-Baltique cars. 
And it is no ordinary gold.  The precious metal comes from gold coins minted between 1908 and 1912.
The flask stopper is capped with  white and yellow gold diamond-encrusted replica of the Russian Imperial Eagle. 
The 1.7 litre bottle inside the flask is crafted with 30 cm thick bulletproof glass. 
It is being created and sold by Latvian owned luxury armoured car company Dartz.
